title: The Fall of Kiev
subtitle: German entry into Kiev and the unfinished pocket battle
author: R.G. Cruise
phase: III — The Battle for Strategic Objectives
summary: German forces entered Kiev; the occupation began while the wider battle against encircled Soviet armies continued.
outlineTopics: German operations leading to the capture of Kiev.
German entry into the city on September 19.
The fate of Soviet formations still trapped east of the city.
The position of the Southwestern Front command.
German attempts to reduce the encircled Soviet armies.
Soviet breakout efforts and their difficulties.
The role of German artillery, infantry, and armored formations.
Soviet demolition of infrastructure during withdrawal.
The immediate establishment of German military control in the city.
The experiences of Kiev's civilian population.
Jewish civilians remaining in the city.
The beginning of German occupation policies and security operations.
The difference between capturing the city and completing the wider encirclement battle.
researchStatus: Editorial outline and date association established. Full researched narrative, claim-level citations and the dated military situation remain to be written and reconstructed.
referenceMapStatus: Candidate German General Staff plate from the supplied chronological sequence. The plate title/date, operational content and reuse conditions have not been independently verified for digitisation.
chronologyNotes: The city was entered on 19 September. Babyn Yar began on 29 September; the wider pocket remained active after Kiev fell.
